title: BMR Calculator: how it works, formula and examples
excerpt: BMR Calculator: Basal metabolic rate — calories burned at rest. Learn how to use it, the formula behind it, a worked example and answers to common questions.
content:
The [BMR Calculator](/bmr-calculator) is a free online tool on CalcHub. Basal metabolic rate — calories burned at rest. Enter your sex, age, weight and height and the result appears straight away — no account or download needed. Because it runs entirely in your browser, the values you type never leave your device, and you can use it as often as you like.

Your Basal Metabolic Rate is the energy your body needs at complete rest to keep you alive — breathing, circulation and cell repair. It typically makes up 60–70% of daily calorie burn. This guide explains how to use it, the formula it applies, and a worked example you can follow with your own numbers. Related Health & Fitness tools include [BMI Calculator](/bmi-calculator), [Calorie Calculator](/calorie-calculator) and [Body Fat Calculator](/body-fat-calculator).

## How to use the BMR Calculator

Start by choosing your sex from the list, then entering your age, entering your weight (kg) and finally entering your height (cm). The result updates as you type, so adjust any value and watch the answer change. If the answer is not what you expected, check the value you entered first — a missing digit or a wrong unit is the usual cause. When you want a clean slate, Reset restores the defaults.

1. Choose your sex from the list.
2. Enter your age.
3. Enter your weight (kg).
4. Enter your height (cm).
5. Check the result — it updates instantly as you type.
6. Use Reset to start over with the default values.

## Formula

Mifflin-St Jeor: Men = 10W + 6.25H − 5A + 5; Women = 10W + 6.25H − 5A − 161 (W kg, H cm, A years).

That is the standard formula for this calculation, and it is the same one the [BMR Calculator](/bmr-calculator) applies to the values you enter. You can work it out by hand, but the calculator is faster when you want to try several values, and it removes the risk of a slip in the arithmetic. If the figures look wrong, check your inputs first — a misplaced decimal point is the usual culprit.

## Worked example

Here is a typical example. A 30-year-old man weighing 75 kg at 178 cm has a BMR of about 1,743 kcal per day. Try the same figures in the [BMR Calculator](/bmr-calculator) and you will get the same result — then change one value at a time to see how the answer moves. The steps are the same whatever numbers you use; only the figures change.

## What the result shows

With the default values (Sex: Male, Age: 30, Weight: 75 kg, Height: 178 cm), the [BMR Calculator](/bmr-calculator) returns BMR: 1,718 kcal/day, Per hour: 72 kcal. The first figure is the headline result, and the rest break it down so you can see how the total is made up. Change any value and every figure updates instantly. If you want to compare with a related calculation, the [BMI Calculator](/bmi-calculator) is worth a look before you finish.

## Tips

A few things worth knowing before you rely on the result — most of them are about the numbers you put in, rather than the tool itself:

- Multiply BMR by an activity factor to get daily needs.
- Building muscle raises BMR slightly.

Keep these in mind and the figures will be as useful as the numbers you put in.

## Frequently asked questions

### BMR vs RMR?

They're very similar; RMR is measured under less strict conditions and is usually slightly higher. Try it with your own numbers in the [BMR Calculator](/bmr-calculator) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.

### Why does BMR fall with age?

Mainly due to loss of lean muscle mass over time. Try it with your own numbers in the [BMR Calculator](/bmr-calculator) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.

### What formula does the BMR Calculator use?

Mifflin-St Jeor: Men = 10W + 6.25H − 5A + 5; Women = 10W + 6.25H − 5A − 161 (W kg, H cm, A years). You can see it in action in the [BMR Calculator](/bmr-calculator) — enter your own values and the result updates as you type.

### What do I need to use the BMR Calculator?

Just Sex, Age, Weight and Height. Enter those values and the result appears straight away — no account or download needed. If you are unsure about a value, try a rough figure first and then refine it — the result updates instantly.
